extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York; voters and politically engaged readers considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting or evaluating public political essays arguing for constitutional provisions (here: taxation and representation) aimed at a general but politically engaged readership. Focus is on justifying institutional design choices and rebutting objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent jurisdiction in taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: "A CONCURRENT JURISDICTION in the article of taxation was the only admissible substitute for an entire subordination, in respect to this branch of power, of State authority to that of the Union."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent jurisdiction reconciles an indefinite constitutional power of taxation in the Federal government with an adequate and independent power in the States to provide for their own necessities; any separation of revenue objects would sacrifice the interests of the Union to State power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid restricting federal revenue to imports
rubrics_metrics.description: If the jurisdiction of the national government in revenue were restricted to particular objects (e.g., duties on imports), it would occasion oppression of particular branches of industry and an unequal distribution of taxes among States and citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confinement to import duties would tempt government (for want of other resources) to extend duties to injurious excess, encourage smuggling, confer premature monopolies on manufacturing states, and create inequality between manufacturing and non-manufacturing States (New York would suffer).

rubrics_metrics.name: National revenues must include internal taxes (excises and direct taxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying solely on import duties is inadequate; recourse must be had to excises and internal taxes to make States contribute in proportion to abilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excises (particular kinds of manufactures) are necessary to reach a fair contribution from States with different manufacturing capacities; internal resources allow a more equitable distribution of burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest of the revenue is a guard against excessive duties, but only when other resources exist
rubrics_metrics.description: The interest of the revenue itself would guard against exorbitant duties so long as other resources were open; if avenues to other resources were closed, necessity would breed harmful experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity can produce false hopes and measures that appear effective at first (e.g., high duties), but later incentives to evade (smuggling) and adverse effects will follow; having multiple revenue options restrains abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overconcentration of taxation on particular objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Limiting federal taxation to particular objects leads to an undue proportion of public burdens falling upon those objects, oppressing specific branches and producing inequality among States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad revenue power prevents concentrating burdens on a narrow set of objects and avoids granting special advantage (or monopoly) to particular industries or states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation need not include members from every occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of actual representation of all classes of the people, by persons of each class, is altogether visionary; mechanics and manufacturers will commonly give votes to merchants who best promote their interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent an express constitutional requirement, expecting each occupation to have its own representative is impractical; natural patrons (e.g., merchants) will serve as representatives for related classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative body will naturally consist of three principal classes
rubrics_metrics.description: From natural operation the representative body will consist almost entirely of proprietors of land, of merchants, and of members of the learned professions, who will truly represent different interests and views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three descriptions of men are seen as able to understand and attend to the feelings and interests of the community (landholders for landed interest, merchants for manufacturing/artisan interests, learned professions as impartial arbiters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of representatives rests on qualifications and dependence on constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate dependent on the suffrages of his fellow-citizens will take care to inform himself of their dispositions and inclinations; this dependence is a chord of sympathy between representative and constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence for taxation administration requires extensive information and acquaintance with the country's genius, habits, modes of thinking, and resources; such qualifications are more important than exact occupational mirroring.

rubrics_metrics.name: National legislature can obtain necessary local knowledge from state representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of local circumstances (as applied to taxation) can be acquired in the national legislature from the representatives of each State; the men sent will generally be able to communicate necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local, minute details are not required at the legislative level; general acquaintance with a State's situation, agriculture, commerce, manufactures, products, and wealth suffice, and specific local execution can be delegated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of local taxes must be delegated to discreet local officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Land taxes are commonly laid by actual valuations or occasional assessments; the execution, which requires knowledge of local details, must be devolved upon discreet persons as commissioners or assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law should name persons or prescribe manner, numbers, and qualifications; national legislature can adopt each State's existing system of assessment and collection for practical execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government may use State systems and officers to collect taxes to avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: In many cases the United States will either abstain from objects preoccupied for local purposes or will make use of the State officers and State regulations for collecting the additional imposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using State officers saves expense, avoids disgust toward State governments, prevents double sets of revenue officers, and can turn State influence toward the Union rather than creating conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment by numbers and a census prevents partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of certain taxes is to be determined by the numbers of each State (second section of first article); an actual census or enumeration must furnish the rule, shutting the door to partiality or oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population-based apportionment is a structural safeguard against arbitrary or partial taxation by the national legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity clause: 'all duties, imposts, and excises shall be UNIFORM throughout the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of duties across the United States is a constitutional provision intended to prevent partial or oppressive revenue schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity, together with apportionment by numbers and use of state systems, operates as a guarded circumspetion against abuse of internal taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal internal taxation preferred to requisitions when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the exercise of internal taxation by the Union should be convenient, it will be preferable because it will be more effectual than relying solely on requisitions to the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of federal taxing power also strengthens the efficacy of requisitions by giving the Union an independent option, thereby motivating States to exert themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double taxation objection answered: total burden is independent of which government levies it
rubrics_metrics.description: The wants of the Union are to be supplied one way or another; if supplied by federal authority, it will not be done by the State authority, so the quantity of taxes to the community must be the same in either case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal exercise of revenue can better utilize convenient branches (commercial imposts) and thus reduce the need for more burdensome taxes, tending to protect poorer classes from oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poll taxes are objectionable but the federal power to impose them should be retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Poll taxes (capitation) are disapproved and lamentable, but the mere existence of the power to lay them does not imply they will be used; nevertheless, in certain emergencies they may be essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because extraordinary contingencies may require unusual expedients, the government should retain the option to employ a poll tax in dire emergencies; several States possess but do not use this power.
